literal: the job-title word; nővér ('sister') is the everyday address term but doubles as the kinship word, so ápoló was chosen to say the sentence unambiguously
Hungarian has no age-neutral everyday word for 'brother' (báty/öcs split on older/younger); fitestvér ('male sibling') is the established word that does not force a choice of relative age
same reasoning as this-is-my-brother -- nőtestvér avoids the néni/húg older/younger split
élettárs is the standard Hungarian word for an unmarried life partner (also the term used in family law), not a business partner
